title: Tools for Development
author: Ok-Way-9449
selftext: Just a quick survey, as you use AI to create your game, do you create any tools as you get into the development.  I have few but have been thinking on this a little bit lately.  My game is a BattleHeart style combat and movement but with small story line that needs more work.  I am at end of 1st half of my ai game development journey and it been a very fun learning curve,  I went from sprites to 2D parts and rigs when I saw sprites would make the game too large for a phone version and even did some interesting tests using Bluestak 5 and my phone.  Done ranting for now.

comments.author: Ok-Way-9449
comments.body:
My game uses rigs also called bones or paperdoll rigging for a web browser based game for testing.  I have the AI create test page that allows the characters to be viewed and all animations plus I found I needed to add  a speed control to slow things down so I can see where gaps are that need to be worked.  It also allows me to place new art on the rig to create a new character of swap out weapons and armor.

When setting up a scene I have the ai create a test page and give me controls to postion background items, enemies/monsters where I want the vs using ai time to have the ai tune the scene.  Also I have used it to set boundries where I don't want players or monsters to go.  You get everything set where you want it and it will download the settings to a json file that I feed back to the ai.

Right now I am trying to create an automated tool that will take a image break it apart and add a rig and basic animations..  If I get it working to where anyone can use it I will make it availabe to everyone.

I am in the early stages and I am feeding info to the AI to make better cuts that are usable.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
I think I've spent as much time making bespoke Unity gizmos as I have implementing systems.

I cannot imagine making a game with absolutely no debugging tools or build assistance.  And that's before all the hours I've sunk into experimenting with custom asset creation pipelines
